Braun RT 20 table radio, 1963

Dieter Rams’s table radio for Braun: a white steel face, tilted slightly back, with a circle of slots for the speaker and a column of grey knobs.

Source
Victoria and Albert Museum, W.13-2007
Creator
Dieter Rams, designer; Braun AG, manufacturer
Made
1963
Style
Ulm School (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Calm, precise, quiet
Evidence
Inspected the V&A’s primary image 2007BR3160 of object W.13-2007 at 1600 × 1067 px, through the V&A IIIF service.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The V&A describes an “oblong beechwood box with a white powder-coated sheet steel fascia tilted slightly backwards”, pierced with slots that form a circular loudspeaker, and says the speaker is concealed “with only pierced lines to indicate its presence”. V&A W.13-2007.

The record transcribes the control labels in lowercase German: “höhen, tiefen, volumen, ein aus, phono, lang, mittel, ukw, sender”. V&A.

Observed

  • The front is one flat white panel inside a pale wood box. Its edge folds over the top with a small radius.
  • On the left, horizontal black slots of different lengths form a circle, split by a narrow vertical gap.
  • Three grey cylindrical knobs stand in a column in the centre, with a tiny label above each. Five small grey push buttons and one larger knob form a row along the bottom.
  • A tall, narrow tuning scale on the right carries fine black numerals and one red horizontal line, the only color on the face.
  • A small black “braun” logo sits above the knob column.

Why it belongs

The RT 20 shows the style’s one-signal rule: grey and white everywhere, and red only where the user reads the station.

Borrow

Draw a circle from parallel lines of different lengths instead of a filled shape.

Give one thin line the only accent color, where the user reads a value.
